# Authoring guide — CustomPresentations

**Guide for engine v@@ENGINE_VERSION@@.** Generated by `tools/build.py` from `engine/AUTHORING.src.md`; do not edit `AUTHORING.md` directly.

This guide is for you and for AI models that create or edit a presentation. Every presentation is a
project folder in `CustomPresentations/presentations/`, like this:

```
presentations/MyTalk/
├── MyTalk_presentation.html     ← the deck (one file: slides + engine + fonts + KaTeX, works offline)
├── Model_animations.html        ← 0…n animation files (optional)
├── images/                      ← every image the deck uses
├── CLAUDE.md                    ← pointer for AI agents (not part of the submission)
└── AUTHORING.md                 ← copy of this guide for this deck's engine version (not submitted)
```

The folder is **self-contained**: it never depends on the CustomPresentations repository. Keep all
files inside it (no `../`, no absolute paths, no URLs); the deck warns about anything else.

---

## 1. Workflow

All tools live in the CustomPresentations repository (`tools/`) and work on any deck folder.
`TOOLS.html` in the repository lists every command and in-browser helper with examples.

| Step | Command |
|---|---|
| Create a presentation in `presentations/<name>` (asks for title, course, animation names …) | `python tools/new.py [name]` |
| Add another animation later (creates the file, registers it in `DECK.animations`) | `python tools/add_animation.py <folder> "Name"` |
| Edit `<prefix>_presentation.html` (only the **user zone**, see §2) | — |
| After adding/changing images: write their sizes into `<img>` tags | `python tools/image_sizes.py <deck.html>` |
| Check the deck (problems per slide and step, image sizes, engine version) | `python tools/check.py <deck.html or folder>` |
| Look at it: open the deck in Chrome/Edge; with `?dev` for problems + components | `…_presentation.html?dev` |
| Bring an older deck to the newest engine (keeps your content) | `python tools/update.py <folder>` |
| Create the zip to submit (only presentation files, verified offline; written next to the folder) | `python tools/pack.py <folder>` |

**Rules for AI agents**
- Before editing, compare engine versions: the deck's is in its `<!-- DECK-ENGINE:BEGIN vX.Y.Z` marker,
  this guide's is at the top. If the deck is older, run `tools/update.py` on the folder first.
- Edit only the user zone. Never edit or read past `<!-- DECK-ENGINE:BEGIN …` (≈1 MB of generated
  code and base64 fonts on very long lines). Never hand-edit vendored or generated files.
- Reuse the components of §7 instead of writing new CSS. Put unavoidable presentation-specific CSS
  into `<style id="deck-user-styles">`.
- After every change run `python tools/check.py <deck>`; fix every reported problem.
- Every `<img>` needs `width`/`height` = the image's natural pixel size (run `tools/image_sizes.py`).

---

## 2. File anatomy

```html
<head>
  <!-- USER ZONE -->
  <style id="deck-user-styles"> /* presentation-specific CSS, always wins */ </style>
  <script id="deck-config"> const DECK = { … }; </script>
</head>
<body>
  <main id="deck"> <section data-type="…"> … </section> … </main>
  <!-- END USER ZONE -->
  <!-- DECK-ENGINE:BEGIN v@@ENGINE_VERSION@@ | generated … --> … <!-- DECK-ENGINE:END -->
</body>
```

The canvas is **1280 × 800** px (16:10), scaled to the screen. Design every slide for that size.

---

## 3. The `DECK` config

```js
const DECK = {
  title:     'EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks',
  subtitle:  'Mingxing Tan, Quoc V. Le (2019)',          // optional
  presenter: 'Simon Meier',
  course:    { title: '252-4811-00L Machine Learning', type: 'Seminar', semester: 'FS26' },
  cover:     { background: 'images/eth_zurich_aerial.png', boxMaxWidth: '58%' },
  toc:       ['Motivation', { text: 'Method', sub: ['Observations', 'Scaling rule'] }, 'Results'],
  animations: [ { id: 'scaling', name: 'Model Scaling', file: 'Model_animations.html' } ],
  date:      'auto',                                    // or a fixed string like '24.04.2026'
  canvas:    { width: 1280, height: 800 },
  hooks:     {},                                        // per-slide JS, rarely needed (§5)
};
```

The title slide and the table of contents are rendered from these values. TOC entries may contain
`$…$` math.

---

## 4. Slides

Each slide is a `<section>` inside `<main id="deck">`; file order = presentation order.

| `data-type` | Where | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | first | empty — rendered from `DECK` |
| `toc` | second | empty — rendered from `DECK.toc` |
| `content` | anywhere after the TOC | your HTML; starts with `<h2 class="slide-title">…</h2>` |
| `animation` | anywhere after the TOC | empty: `data-anim="<id>"`, optional `data-params="phi=3"`, required `data-title="…"` |
| `black` | exactly one, after the main slides | empty (end of the talk) |

Slides after the black slide are the **appendix** ("Appendix 1, 2, …"). Numbers, footer, date,
ETH logo and the navigator are automatic. Optional section attributes: `id="…"` (for hooks/links),
`data-layout="center"` (centred content) or `"full"` (no padding), `data-bg-color="#f5f3ee"`.

**A complete content slide** (title on arrival, figure with click 1, red marker with click 2, the
unmarked conclusion last):

```html
<section data-type="content" id="results">
  <h2 class="slide-title">Results – <span class="title-mark">fewer parameters</span></h2>
  <div class="figure-wrap" data-step="1">
    <div class="figure">
      <img src="images/results.png" width="1600" height="720" alt="Accuracy vs. parameters">
      <div class="overlay-line" style="top: 20%" data-step="2" data-step-fx="fade"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="conclusion-box">Same accuracy with 8× fewer parameters</div>
</section>
```
This slide has four steps: 0 (title), 1 (figure), 2 (red line), 3 (conclusion box).

---

## 5. Steps (0-based)

- **Step 0** = the slide title + everything marked `data-step="0"` (shown on arrival).
- **Steps 1 … k** = what you assign: `data-step="2"` (from step 2 on), `data-step="1..2"` (steps 1–2,
  removed at 3), `data-step="3..3"` (only at step 3).
- **One final step** shows everything **unmarked**. A slide without numbered steps has two steps:
  title → everything. If everything is assigned, there is no extra final step.
- Unmarked containers that hold stepped elements stay visible; the rule applies inside them:
  `<ul><li>A</li><li data-step="0">B</li><li data-step="2">C</li></ul>` → B at 0, C at 2, A last.
- Classes per step instead of show/hide: `data-step-class="hi:1..1 bold:2"` (`.hi` only at step 1,
  `.bold` from step 2).
- Reveal effect: `data-step-fx="rise"` (default) | `fade` | `slide-left` | `none`.
- → / Space / PageDown / ↓ go forward, ← / PageUp / ↑ back. Each slide remembers its step.
- Rare: `data-steps="5"` declares the number of steps for a slide driven by a hook
  (`DECK.hooks['slide-id'] = (step, slideEl, ctx) => {}`).

---

## 6. Images, math and code

- `<img src="images/x.png" width="1600" height="900" alt="">` — `width`/`height` are the natural
  size (`tools/image_sizes.py` fills them); scale with CSS (`style="width: 400px"`), the aspect ratio
  is kept automatically.
- Background images: `<div data-bg="images/x.png" data-bg-size="contain">` — never CSS `url(…)`.
- A missing image shows a white box `image "x.png" not found` at the right size, never a broken slide.
- Math: `$…$` inline, `$$…$$` display (KaTeX, offline). A literal dollar sign: `\$`.
- Code: `<pre class="code-block" data-lang="python">…</pre>` is coloured automatically; other
  languages use the token classes `.ck .cf .ca .cn .cs .cc`.

## 8. Animations

- Start every animation from `template_animations.html`: `tools/new.py` does this when you name an
  animation, `tools/add_animation.py <folder> "Name"` adds one to an existing project (file + entry in
  `DECK.animations`). Keep its `ANIM-VENDOR` and `ANIM-CONTRACT` blocks: without the contract the deck shows
  `animation "x.html" not found`.
- **Panels** (as in the EfficientNet animation): each sidebar card `<div class="scard" data-panel="ID">`
  belongs to one `<div class="panel" data-panel="ID">`. Clicking a card opens/closes its panel; at most
  **3** panels are open, a 4th closes the one opened longest ago; open panels always appear in **sidebar
  order**. Draw with `Panels.onDraw('ID', fn)` (called after opening and on resize; `Panels.redraw()` after
  a parameter change). Slides open panels with `data-params="open=ID1,ID2"`; without `open` the first
  panel is shown.
- Register it: `DECK.animations: [{ id: 'model', name: 'Model scaling', file: 'Model_animations.html' }]`.
  One animation → `▶ Animation` toggles it; several → `▶ Animations` opens a picker.
- Show it as a slide: `<section data-type="animation" data-anim="model" data-params="phi=2" data-title="…"></section>`.
  The animation reads `data-params` from its URL (`readURLParams()`) or via `window.applyPreset(cfg)`.
- Arrow keys inside an animation move the presentation; Ctrl/Shift + arrows stay in the animation.
- **Animation steps (D / A keys, as in games):** **D** = one step forward, **A** = one step back — in the
  deck on an animation slide or with the animation open, or inside the animation. They call
  `window.animStep(dir)` of the visible animation (`dir` = `1` or `-1`): steps of the animation itself,
  while Space/arrows keep moving the slides. Define it in the animation, e.g.
  `window.animStep = dir => { step = Math.min(LAST, Math.max(0, step + dir)); redraw(); };`
  (the starter's demo: D / A = next / previous φ). Without `window.animStep`, D and A do nothing.

---

## 9. Checking and submitting

- `?dev` in the URL: the ☰ Slides navigator lists every problem per slide (with its step; click to
  jump), deck-wide problems in a red box; **▦ Components** shows all components.
- `python tools/check.py <folder>` prints the same problems plus image-size and engine-version
  issues; exit code 1 if anything needs fixing.
- `python tools/pack.py <folder>` writes `<prefix>.zip` (next to the folder, e.g. `presentations/MyTalk.zip`)
  with only what the presentation uses: the deck, the files it names (animations in `DECK.animations`,
  images, links) and the files those name (an animation's images), after verifying a copy works offline
  outside the repository. Unused files are listed as left out. If code builds a file name
  (`'images/frame' + i + '.png'`), write each path out once (e.g. in an array), or it is not packed.
- `presentations/EfficientNet/` is a complete example project (the original EfficientNet talk rebuilt):
  look there for how slides, steps, components and animation slides are written.
- Updating: `python tools/update.py <folder>` replaces only the generated engine blocks (backups
  `*.bak`) and refreshes `AUTHORING.md` / `CLAUDE.md`. Within 1.x updates never change the meaning
  of existing attributes or config; a breaking change would be 2.0 with migration notes here.

---

## 10. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `image "x.png" not found` (white box) | File missing from `images/` or path/name differs. Fix it, run `tools/image_sizes.py`. |
| `animation "x.html" not found` | File missing, name differs from `DECK.animations`, or its `ANIM-CONTRACT` block was removed. |
| `… points outside the presentation folder` | A path uses `../`, an absolute path or a URL; copy the file into the folder. |
| Red formula / `formula error` | KaTeX cannot parse it (message in `check.py`). Literal dollar: `\$`. |
| Content appears a click too early/late | Steps are 0-based; unmarked content comes last (§5). Check with `?dev` → ☰ Slides. |
| `has no width/height attributes` | Run `tools/image_sizes.py <deck>`. |
| `title slide content is ignored` | The cover is built from `DECK`; leave `<section data-type="title">` empty. |
| Text smaller than expected | The browser is not fullscreen; press F11 (the slide is a fixed 1280×800 canvas). |
| Anything in the engine block edited by mistake | `tools/update.py <folder>` rewrites the generated blocks; the slides stay untouched. |

## 11. Asking an AI assistant

Give it the project folder (its `CLAUDE.md` points here) and concrete requests, e.g.
"add a slide with the results table from `notes.md`, highlight our model's rows, reveal the
conclusion on the last click", then let it run `tools/check.py`. Ask it to reuse the components
of §7 and to keep all files inside the project folder.
